newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian searchers look for second yachtsman.
newsitem.headline: Australian searchers look for second yachtsman.

text.p: An Australian search plane was scouring the Southern Ocean late on Monday for a missing round-the-world yachtsman after earlier dropping life rafts to a second solo sailor found on his upturned yacht.

One of the two yachts was spotted capsized with a survivor clinging to its hull in freezing seas shortly after 1 p.m. local time (0500 GMT), about 1,400 nautical miles (2,600 kms) southwest of Perth, Australian Maritime Safety Authority spokesman David Gray told Reuters.
Briton Tony Bullimore, 56, on board Global Exide Challenger, and 29-year-old Frenchman Thierry Dubois on board Amnesty International sent out distress calls late on Sunday after sailing into a storm.
An airforce search aircraft was despatched to the region, about four hours' flying time from Perth, and discovered one of the yachts upturned and partly submerged.
The survivor could not be immediately identified.
Australian Defence Force spokesman Colonel Andrew Reynolds told Reuters sea and wind conditions were holding the rafts out of the survivor's reach about 100 metres (yards) from the yacht.
Two packages each containing two rafts connected by ropes were dropped upwind of the survivor shortly before 0830 GMT.
Gray said the crew of the search plane also reported they had mistakenly identified the upturned hull of the second yacht about two nautical miles away from the first boat.
"The position at this time is that only one hull has been found. The other object that was sighted was not a hull," Gray said.

The two competitors in the Vendee Globe round-the-world race hit difficulties about 120 nautical miles (220 kms) south of the region where French yachtsman Raphael Dinelli was rescued from his sinking yacht two days after Christmas.
The airforce plane carried enough fuel to maintain the search for about four hours, and would shortly be replaced by a second plane, Reynolds said.
"The captain of the second plane will decide whether to drop more rafts and will also attempt to drop communication equipment to the yachtsman so we can identify him," Reynolds said.
The second plane will also search for the other yachtsman.
A Royal Australian Navy frigate HMAS Adelaide also left Perth at about 4 p.m. local time (0800 GMT) with a Seahawk helicopter, but could take up to three days to reach the area.
Weather conditions, meanwhile, were deteriorating with a heavy swell of six metres and winds of 40-50 knots, ahead of an expected storm, Gray said.
It was the longest rescue Australian maritime authorities had attempted for yachtsmen, he added.
Two years ago Australian officials launched a large-scale rescue mission to save French yachtswoman Isabelle Autissier, who was competing in the BOC Round-the-World Yacht race.
